newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian politicans threatened in race debate.
newsitem.headline: Australian politicans threatened in race debate.

text.p: Australian politicians have received threating and abusive letters after the government and opposition united to condemn racism, a senior parliamentary officer said on Thursday.
House of Representatives Speaker Bob Halverson said he feared the abuse could be an attempt to pressure politicians.
Halverson told parliament that opposition backbencher Andrew Theophanous, a prominent social welfare campaigner, had received a threatening letter and threatening and abusive phone calls.

"He reported to me that he had been informed by other honourable members that following the parliament's passing of the unanimous motion...last week a number of members had received similar letters and telephone calls," Halverson said.
"I share (Theophanous')...concern that this may be a broader phenomenon which poses a challenge to MPs in the performance of their duties," he said.

Amid a heated national debate about racism, the conservative Liberal-National government and the Labor opposition united last week in a parliamentary motion condemning racism and pledging commitment to an open and tolerant society.
Opinion polls have shown widespread support for independent politician Pauline Hanson, whose controversial comments about Asia and immigration sparked the race debate.
Hanson's incorrect warning that Asians were swamping Australia and her call for an immediate halt to immigration have been blamed for a reported rise in complaints of racial discrimination.
Asians make up about 2.7 percent of Australia's 18 million population and about one third of the annual 100,000 immigrants.
